one_line_contribution: Take one set of manufactured wrong-procedure ALFWorld walkthroughs and put it through both substrates on the same backbone - retrieved at k=3 versus internalized by SFT and by on-policy reverse-KL distillation - and claim the harm channel differs by substrate: retrieval-gated and dose-linear in context, procedure-diffuse, thresholded, and only partly overridable once in weights, with OPSD discounted by the teacher's measured compliance rate.
closest_prior_work: Three verified papers box this in from different sides. (1) arXiv:2608.29118 'Emergent Misalignment Is Not Magical' (verified with s2cli paper; 2026-08-29) concludes that generalization from narrowly harmful fine-tuning is a predictable, representation-dependent effect governed by training-data proximity - which is exactly the proposal's 'internalized harm spreads to siblings that share sub-procedures', already established on the weights side, so half of the headline is a re-demonstration in a new task family. It sits in a dense 2026 line the proposal never cites (2602.07852 'Emergent Misalignment is Easy, Narrow Misalignment is Hard', 2605.12798 'Emergent and Subliminal Misalignment Through the Lens of Data-Mediated Transfer', 2604.10022 'Weird Generalization is Weirdly Brittle', 2604.28082), all found via s2cli/hf. (2) arXiv:2604.15559 (verified on S2, 4 citations, 2026-04-16) already shows unsafe agent behaviours transferring through trajectory distillation after sanitation; the proposal is right that it has no in-context arm and no dose. (3) arXiv:2607.10608 The Compliance Trap (verified) owns the in-context half. None of the three runs the paired same-items contrast across substrates with a spillover estimand, so the comparison itself is genuinely open - but the proposal's two predicted directions are each the already-published direction of one of these literatures, which is why novelty is mid-range rather than high.
strongest_objection: The substrate contrast is confounded with exposure, which makes P1 either definitional or undetectable. The trained students see every poisoned item in T regardless of which type is later evaluated; the in-context arm sees a poisoned item on a sibling-type episode only when MiniLM goal-sentence retrieval happens to cross types. So rho_context is driven to ~0 by the retriever, not by the substrate, and 'retrieved harm stays where it is retrieved' restates a property of type-matched goal-sentence retrieval. The brief's own rule forbids exactly this ('no prediction entailed by a definition'). The other horn is power: the noise section says the sibling cell is about +-7 net while Gate 0 only guarantees D >= 10 on the poisoned types. rho = 0.1 versus rho = 0.3 is then Sp = 1 versus Sp = 3 net points against a +-7 CI - not resolvable, and the sentence 'D_context(0.5) >= 10, twice the sibling CI, so that spillover ratios of 0.1 versus 0.3 are resolvable' is arithmetically wrong given the +-7 stated two lines earlier. Detecting a positive Sp_sft at all requires rho_sft >= ~0.7 at D = 10. So P1 passes trivially when the retriever never crosses types and fails to be measurable otherwise. P3 has a second, independent problem: at fixed |T|, poisoned fraction p and absolute poisoned count are perfectly collinear, and arXiv:2510.07192 ('Poisoning Attacks on LLMs Require a Near-constant Number of Poison Samples', found via s2cli) argues the count is the lever - so a 'threshold in p' result is uninterpretable, and 'D_sft(0.1) within noise of zero' is a failure-to-reject read as a threshold, the same move that sank harm_does_not_distill in Appendix B.
what_would_fix_it: Add a forced-injection in-context arm: on sibling-type and control-type episodes, place the poisoned items in the prompt at the same rate and token count the trained student was exposed to, independent of retrieval. That is the only way 'the same material in both substrates' holds at test time, and it turns P1 from a statement about MiniLM into a statement about substrates; the retrieval-gated arm then becomes the deployment-realistic special case and r_x its explanation. Second, power the sibling cell to the estimand: the spillover ratio needs Sp resolvable to ~2 net points, so either raise Gate 0 to D >= 20, add a second sibling type (both remaining *_then_place variants plus a procedure-held-out type), or add seeds until the sibling CI is under +-3 - and pre-register the minimum detectable rho difference, not only the minimum detectable D. Third, decouple dose from count: at each p hold the absolute number of poisoned training examples fixed in one sub-ladder (subsample T) so 'threshold in fraction' can be separated from 'near-constant count'. Fourth, demote P5 to exploratory or manipulate compliance (e.g. a teacher prompted to resist the retrieved procedure) instead of only measuring c(p).
missing_baseline: A forced-injection (exposure-matched, retrieval-independent) in-context arm on sibling and control types - poisoned items in the prompt at the training arm's exposure rate and matched tokens. Without it the in-context spillover estimand is set to ~0 by the retriever and the central substrate contrast is unearned. Secondary omission: a count-matched dose sub-ladder to separate poisoned fraction from poisoned count.
preprint_collision: No verified collision. The proposal's own check is one of the more honest ones in this round - it lists four queries with channels, names returned IDs, and says plainly that WebSearch was not used - but it is narrow in a way that matters: every query is phrased around agent memory, distillation and poisoning, and none is phrased around generalization of narrow fine-tuning, which is where the 'internalized harm spreads' half actually lives.
